Finn headed into the creative arena (battlefield).

rivaling any battle in the Dungeon—
t7085:
The main screen where you can access every feature.
Peek into the daily lives of Bell, Hestia,
and many other characters.
Discover sides of them you don't usually see.
t7086:
The screen where you choose battles to play.
Experience the DanMachi tale in "Story,"
gather materials in "Daily," enjoy limited-time
"Events," and set out on all kinds
of adventures.
t7087:
The screen for battling other players.
Choose between Magic Stone Scramble and Arena Tournament.
t7088:
The screen for checking tasks given to the player.
Clear tasks to receive various rewards.
t7089:
The screen where you can buy Magic Gems and
great-value item packs. The cheerful, lovely staff of
The Benevolent Mistress greet you when you enter.
t7090:
The screen for exchanging items
obtained in events and more.
Run by a gentle, ever-smiling shopkeeper,
it offers items available nowhere else.
t7091:
The screen for interacting with the people
of Orario. Clear battles together and give
gifts to raise CP. Reach certain ranks to
unlock special stories and rewards.
t7092:
One of the events held at the Arena. Form a
party and battle other players.
Set an attack style when forming your party;
battles play out automatically.
t7093:
One of the events held at the Arena. A battle
for magic stones against 8 players. Rankings are
decided by how many magic stones you hold at the end,
and stones can be traded for items at the Exchange.
t7094:
Raise a character's Mastery.
Upgraded characters gain
HP, Strength, Magic, Endurance, and Dexterity.
t7095:
Unlock a character's Mastery cap.
Unlocking it lets you upgrade
the character even further.
t7096:
Awakening raises a character's rarity.
Higher rarity improves their Ultimate,
Action Skills, and Status.
t7097:
Upgrade adventurer Skills and assists' Assist Skills.
Raising their level increases the power
and effect of Skills/Assist Skills.
t7098:
Battle item traits change every time
you remake the item, so keep trying
until you get the effects you want.
t7099:
Raise a Scene Card's rank.
Higher-ranked Scene Cards have
enhanced Status.
You can also unlock the rank cap.
t7100:
Pink attack warnings used by enemies
follow the adventurer, then lock in place after a while.
Lure them carefully so your
room to move isn't restricted.
t7101:
The currency used throughout Orario. Earned as a
reward for winning battles, among other things.
Used to buy items and to enhance characters, Scene Cards, and more.
t7102:
Having joined the Hestia Familia,
Bell Cranel made his home in a run-down church
deep in a deserted back alley
and devoted himself to the Dungeon.
t7103:
Having finished today's Dungeon exploration
without earning much,
Bell heads home with drooping shoulders.
t7104:
Buoyed by his goddess's words,
Bell made it through the crisis.
In high spirits, he returned to the church.
t7105:
A Minotaur appeared out of nowhere.
The one who saved Bell from certain death
was a Level 5 hailed as one of Orario's strongest—
the Sword Princess, Ais Wallenstein.
After that fateful meeting...the story begins to move.
t7106:
The morning after his Status update,
Bell wakes up and tries to head
to the Dungeon as usual, but...
t7107:
As promised to the waitress he met that morning,
Bell visits The Benevolent Mistress after the Dungeon.
Guided by the waitress,
he steps into the lively tavern.
t7108:
Hestia waited alone in front of the church.
For her one and only follower.
Her most precious, most beloved follower.
t7109:
The underground labyrinth beneath
Labyrinth City Orario. It existed in the mortal world
even before the gods descended,
and is a cauldron of vicious monsters.
t7110:
A huge city built on top of the Dungeon.
It prospers with the Guild at its core, and humans
live alongside demi-humans of every race.
t7111:
The organization that runs Labyrinth City Orario.
It oversees much of Orario, from supporting
adventurers to responding to emergencies.
t7112:
The white skyscraper towering
at the center of Labyrinth City Orario.
It serves as the "lid" on the Dungeon,
and no building in Orario stands taller.
t7113:
The Familia led by its patron goddess Hestia.
Once a tiny Familia, it has drawn attention and stirred up the city thanks to Bell's feats (the fastest Level Up in history, overcoming crisis after crisis, and more).
t7114:
The Familia led by its patron god Loki.
With many first-tier adventurers, such as Captain Finn
the Braver, Ais the Sword Princess, and Riveria
the Nine Hell, it's said to be the city's strongest.
t7115:
The Familia led by its patron god Miach.
Captained by the Chienthrope Nahza, it runs an item shop out of its home, the Blue Pharmacy.
t7116:
The Familia led by its patron god Takemikazuchi.
Captain Ouka, Mikoto, Chigusa, and every other member
hails from the Far East. Small, but truly skilled.
t7117:
The Familia led by its patron goddess Hephaistos.
Its captain is Tsubaki Collbrande, the Cyclops.
Smithing is its trade, and the Familia's name
itself is recognized as a luxury brand.
t7118:
The Familia led by its patron god Hermes.
Its captain is Asfi Al Andromeda, Perseus.
Since Hermes travels all over the world,
the members run the Familia themselves.
t7119:
The Familia led by its patron goddess Freya.
Its captain is Ottar the Warlord,
the city's only Level 7. With many first-tier
adventurers, it's said to rival the Loki Familia,
the city's strongest.
t7120:
The Familia led by its patron goddess Ishtar.
Its captain is Phryne Jamil, the Andro Killer.
Most of its members are Amazons, and its fighters
are called battle prostitutes (Berbera).
t7121:
The Familia led by its patron god Ganesha.
Its captain is Shakti Varma, Ankusha.
With the city's largest membership and many upper-class
adventurers, it's a key keeper of the city's peace.
t7122:
Monsters with intelligence and hearts.
Unlike ordinary monsters, some understand human
speech and can hold conversations. What they all
share is a deep longing for the surface and humanity.
t7123:
A tavern popular with Orario's adventurers.
Bell's acquaintances Syr and Ryu work here.
Apparently it runs as a café until evening, when adventurers return from the Dungeon.
t7124: Also called floor bosses, these special monsters appear alone on specific floors. Their forms vary by floor, but all wield immense power. Adventurers generally take them on in large, coordinated groups.
t7125: Looks like your Stamina's all topped up!
t7131: I got this ready just for you!
t7136: Thank you for always being here!
t7140: If it makes you happy, I'm happy too.
t7143: Just a small token of my thanks.
